Only part 4 of the table is machine-readable and it is expressed per YEAR of combined production, so no per-Nm3 amount can be derived from it; the two items below come from the aggregated-vector block of this prompt.; allocation: Combined gas and oil production is allocated 63.8 % to crude oil and 36.2 % to natural gas (the only numbers the readable part of the table carries).. evidence.source: 2025 - LCI crude oil and natural gas extraction - Meili.pdf

gaps_reported_by_model: Tab. 12.2 parts 1-3 (pages 76-78) are images in the PDF: the text extraction returned only the page headers, so the technosphere inputs, resources and air emissions of the unit process are simply not readable.

Part 4, the only readable page, is printed PER YEAR of combined oil-and-gas production ('Unit' = a) with the country-specific allocation keys 63.8 % (oil) / 36.2 % (gas) shown in place of amounts in the per-kg and per-Nm3 columns. Without the annual production volume - which the excerpt does not give - none of those absolute annual figures can be turned into a per-kg or per-Nm3 amount.

The example is for CANADA; this dataset is a different country, and the report states that only the parameters (energy demand, flaring, methane, produced water, spills) are country-specific, not the exchange structure.
Readable but unusable annual emission rows: oils/BOD5/COD/DOC/TOC/AOX/nitrogen/sulfur to river and to ocean, oils to soil, SO2 and NOx to air, Halon 1301 and HFC-23 to air.
No energy inputs, no drilling or production-plant infrastructure, no flaring, no methane venting could be read.
